items.stem: Which of the following best describes "multiplier"?
options: The change in a quantity as a percentage of its original value: (change ÷ original) × 100%
Two quantities are inversely proportional when their product stays constant, so if one doubles the other halves (y = k/x)
The single number you multiply by to apply a percentage change, e.g. 1.15 for a 15% increase
Two quantities are directly proportional when their ratio stays constant, so if one doubles the other doubles (y = kx)
items.answer: The single number you multiply by to apply a percentage change, e.g. 1.15 for a 15% increase
items.markingKey: C. "multiplier" is the single number you multiply by to apply a percentage change, e.g. 1.15 for a 15% increase.

(a) Write the ratio in its simplest form. (b) Find each share. (c) Freya argues the profit should be shared equally because everyone works the same hours. Comment on this.
items.answer: (a) 5 : 2 : 1 (b) AED 2950, AED 1180, AED 590 (c) a fair argument either way: investment risk versus equal work
items.markingKey: (a) 5 : 2 : 1 (b) AED 2950, AED 1180, AED 590 (c) a fair argument either way: investment risk versus equal work. Ratio simplified/scaled (M1 A1); shares or limiting quantity found (M1 A1); reasoned comment in context (D: R1).

items.stem: A student enterprise in Geneva buys 139 T-shirts at CHF 12 each, pays CHF 90 for printing, and sells them at CHF 15 each. (a) Find the profit if all are sold. (b) Find the percentage profit on total costs. (c) What is the least number they must sell to break even?
items.answer: (a) CHF 327 (b) 18.6% (c) 118 T-shirts
items.markingKey: (a) CHF 327 (b) 18.6% (c) 118 T-shirts. Percentages/interest calculated (M1 A1); totals compared (M1 A1); justified recommendation in context (D: R1 C1).

items.stem: Which multiplier decreases an amount by 8%?
items.markingKey: D. 92% of the amount = 0.92 × amount.

items.stem: Which set of (x, y) pairs shows y directly proportional to x?
items.markingKey: A. In (2, 8), (3, 12), (4, 16) the ratio y/x is always 4.

items.stem: Which ratio is equivalent to 1 : 5?
items.markingKey: B. Multiply both parts by 9.

items.stem: Explain why simple interest grows by the same amount each year.
items.answer: Interest is always calculated on the original principal, which does not change, so each year adds P × r/100.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Interest is always calculated on the original principal, which does not change, so each year adds P × r/100. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: A shop increases a price by 25% and later decreases the new price by 20%. Mateo says the overall change is +5%. Explain whether Mateo is correct and find the true overall percentage change.
items.answer: Not correct: multiplier 1.25 × 0.8 = 1, an overall change of 0%.
items.markingKey: Percentages of different amounts cannot simply be added (R1); combined multiplier (M1); correct overall change (A1).

items.stem: x: 1, 2, 3, 4; y: 15, 24, 33, 42. y increases by 9 each time. Explain why y is NOT directly proportional to x.
items.answer: y/x is not constant (15/1 = 15, 24/2 = 12); when x = 0, y = 6, not 0.
items.markingKey: Ratio test or intercept argument (R1 R1); clear conclusion (C1).

items.stem: Jonas says that adding 5 to both parts of 1 : 7 gives an equivalent ratio. Explain, with a numerical check, why this is wrong.
items.answer: 6 : 12 ≠ 1 : 7, because 1/2 ≠ 1/7; equivalent ratios multiply or divide both parts by the same number.
items.markingKey: Counter-check with values (A1); correct rule stated (R1).

items.stem: A student claims: "Simple interest of 5% for 4 years means the money is multiplied by 5 × 4 = 20." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: The interest is 5% × 4 = 20% of the principal, so the total is 1.2 × the principal.
items.markingKey: The interest is 5% × 4 = 20% of the principal, so the total is 1.2 × the principal. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: A shop increases a price by 10% and later decreases the new price by 25%. Ana says the overall change is −15%. Explain whether Ana is correct and find the true overall percentage change.
items.answer: Not correct: multiplier 1.1 × 0.75 = 0.825, an overall decrease of 17.5%.
items.markingKey: Percentages of different amounts cannot simply be added (R1); combined multiplier (M1); correct overall change (A1).

items.stem: 3 metres of rope cost C$4.08 in Toronto. Find the cost of 7 metres of rope.
Write the three-part ratio 45 : 9 : 18 in its simplest form, and then in the form 1 : n : p.
items.markingKey: Divide by the HCF 9 (M1 A1); divide all parts by 5 for the unit form (A1).

items.stem: Tariq invests S$500 at 6% simple interest per year. Find the total value of the investment after 5 years.
items.markingKey: Interest S$150.00 (M1 A1); total S$650.00 (A1).

items.stem: The price of a concert ticket in Singapore changed from S$76 to S$71. Calculate the percentage decrease, to 1 decimal place where necessary.
items.markingKey: Change = S$5 (M1); ÷ original 76 × 100 (M1); 6.6% (A1).

items.stem: A journey takes 10 hours at 30 km/h. How long would it take at 50 km/h?
items.answer: 6 hours
items.markingKey: Inverse proportion: total (speed × time) = 3 × 10 = 30 (M1); ÷ 5 = 6 hours (A1).

items.stem: Paint is mixed from blue and white in the ratio 7 : 5. The mixture contains 36 mL more blue than white. Find the total volume of paint.
items.answer: 216 mL
items.markingKey: Difference of 2 parts = 36 mL (M1), so 1 part = 18 mL (A1); total 12 parts = 216 mL (A1).

items.stem: In a sale in Lisbon, second-hand bicycles marked at €248 are reduced by 25%. The shop paid €148.80 for each. Find (a) the sale price, (b) the percentage profit on the cost price.

A phone costs AED 436 before tax. A sales tax of 8% is added and then a 7% discount is given on the price with tax. (a) Find the final price. (b) Would the customer pay less if the discount were applied before the tax? Justify your answer.
items.answer: (a) AED 438.42 (b) no – the order does not matter, because multiplication is commutative: 1.08 × 0.93 = 0.93 × 1.08
items.markingKey: (a) AED 438.42 (b) no – the order does not matter, because multiplication is commutative: 1.08 × 0.93 = 0.93 × 1.08. Multipliers used correctly (M1 M1); accurate answers (A1 A1); reasoning in context communicated (D: R1).

items.stem: Jonas travels from Vienna to Nairobi. The exchange rate is 1 euro = 139.1 Kenyan shillings. (a) How many Kenyan shillings does Jonas get for 220 euros? (b) On return, Jonas changes 38940 Kenyan shillings back. How many euros is that, to 2 d.p.? (c) Explain why exchange rate conversions are an example of direct proportion.
items.answer: (a) 30602.00 Kenyan shillings (b) 279.94 euros (c) amount received = rate × amount changed, a constant multiplier (graph through origin)
items.markingKey: (a) 30602.00 Kenyan shillings (b) 279.94 euros (c) amount received = rate × amount changed, a constant multiplier (graph through origin). Type of proportion identified (R1); unitary or product method (M1 A1); second calculation (A1); assumption or interpretation (D: R1).

items.stem: A bread recipe uses flour and water in the ratio 7 : 3 by mass. (a) How much water is needed for 490 g of flour? (b) Ana has 419 g of flour and 300 g of water. Which ingredient runs out first, and what is the greatest total mass of dough (flour + water) they can make?
items.answer: (a) 210 g (b) flour runs out first; dough 598.6 g
items.markingKey: (a) 210 g (b) flour runs out first; dough 598.6 g. Ratio simplified/scaled (M1 A1); shares or limiting quantity found (M1 A1); reasoned comment in context (D: R1).
